Maya (solutions): Quick sync on the Stark POC — Splunk shows request_id but no trace_id/traceparent. Can we triage?
Dev (infra): Classic chain: client -> ALB -> WAF -> nginx -> app -> forwarder -> Splunk HEC. Which header are you sending?
Maya (solutions): We send x-redwood-trace and traceparent. ALB logs have them but Splunk events don't.
Ravi (sales-eng): Customer says WAF policies are strict and they suspect it strips unknown headers. They can't change WAF during business hours.
Dev (infra): Two fast options: 1) switch to a WAF-allowed header like x-request-id and map it to trace_id in the forwarder, 2) synthesize trace_id from request_id in the forwarder if headers absent. Option 1 preserves real propagation, option 2 is a POC fallback.
Maya (solutions): How would the forwarder remap look?
Dev (infra): Example Vector remap (pseudo): 
  .trace_id = if exists(.headers["x-redwood-trace"]) { .headers["x-redwood-trace"] } else if exists(.headers["x-request-id"]) { .headers["x-request-id"] } else null
And a synth fallback: 
  if not .trace_id and .request_id then .trace_id = .request_id end
Ravi (sales-eng): Customer asks: will synthesizing break trace trees or compliance?
Dev (infra): It won't reconstruct parent/child relationships — it only gives you a common id to join logs/spans for dashboards. Compliance: no extra PII introduced; redaction still runs. We can provide a config snapshot showing REDWOOD_REDACT_FIELDS during the POC.
observability-bot: alert: forwarder.stark.hec spike - 2026-03-20T23:12Z -> 20m (avg 6/min) HTTP 429s detected
Maya (solutions): That 429 window corresponds to missing child spans. If HEC rejects events spans get dropped and you see orphaned logs.
Dev (infra): Recommend parallel fixes: A) map to x-request-id or synth transform B) increase forwarder buffering/retries or request HEC bump. Suggested envs: FORWARDER_BUFFER_BYTES=100MB, FORWARDER_RETRIES=5.
Ravi (sales-eng): They worry about duplicates if we enable retries. Any guidance?
Dev (infra): Small duplication possible; for short POC it's acceptable. If needed enable dedupe by hash on HEC or the forwarder. We'll note this in the playbook.
Maya (solutions): Can we provide a short smoke test for SREs to validate after changes?
Dev (infra): Yep: 1) curl -H "x-request-id: poc-abc-01" -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/debug/header-echo -> response should include x-request-id. 2) Splunk search: index=stark trace_id="poc-abc-01" within 60s.
Ravi (sales-eng): Customer has a midnight maintenance window and will either allow WAF rule change or accept forwarder remap. I'll capture both options in the ticket and update pricing note (buffering negligible for POC).
Maya (solutions): I'll add the SOC text: "Traces do not contain user PII by default; redaction enabled; correlation headers preserved unless an intermediary rewrites them; playbook provided for POC."
Dev (infra): I'll push the playbook and the Vector remap snippet to the ticket, plus a config snapshot proving redaction envs.
observability-bot: info: playbook release/poc-stark-obsv-playbook rolled at 2026-03-22T00:05Z
Maya (solutions): Verified after WAF change: header echo shows x-redwood-trace in nginx access_log and Splunk events include trace_id. Closing loop.
Ravi (sales-eng): Customer satisfied. Closing thread unless something else shows up. :white_check_mark:
